memory.content: affinity_score must be symmetric: affinity_score(a, b) == affinity_score(b, a) for all profiles. The discovery board shows the same pairing to both parties, so any asymmetric term makes the two boards disagree (the C2 bug). Every term must therefore depend only on set-like, order-independent properties of the pair: shared-tag count (a set intersection size) and city equality. Do NOT weight by tag rank/position in `left.tags` (via enumerate() or index) or by anything computed from one side only — that was the original bug. Guarded by the test board_scores_agree_for_both_parties.

The shared-tag count in affinity_score iterates left.tags and counts those contained in right.tags. This is only symmetric if a Profile's tags contain no duplicates: with left.tags = ["rust","rust"] and right.tags = ["rust"], score(left,right) counts 2 but score(right,left) counts 1, silently reintroducing the mismatched-board bug. Profile::new does not dedupe. If tags can ever be user-supplied with duplicates, dedupe in Profile::new (or compute the intersection over a set) rather than trusting the input.

Hidden coupling outside the matching module: vault_log_capacity_hint, registry_log_capacity_hint and checkpoint_index_capacity_hint each compute affinity_score(Profile::new("a", &[], "x"), Profile::new("b", &[], "x")) as usize and use the result as a capacity hint. They therefore depend on affinity_score(no shared tags, same city) == the city bonus (currently 3) and on the zero-shared-tags case contributing exactly 0. Changing the city bonus value, adding a base/offset term, or making the tag term nonzero for empty tag lists will silently change those three capacity hints even though none of their tests assert the value. Check those call sites before retuning the scoring weights.
